Urban Pulse NYC: EDA and the 15 analyst investigations¶

This notebook is the analysis part of the project. It:

  1. loads the cleaned data and inspects it (shape, types, missing values)
  2. runs the statistics checks: centre, spread, skewness, IQR outliers
  3. answers the 15 analyst questions. Each one shows question, SQL, sample size, chart, pattern, cautious interpretation

The SQL lives in sql/analyst_queries.sql and runs against MySQL (urban_pulse_db.service_requests). Run order for the whole pipeline: src/extract.py → src/clean.py → src/load_mysql.py → this notebook → streamlit run app/streamlit_app.py.

In [1]:

import numpy as np, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, seaborn as sns

2. Statistical checking: centre, spread, skewness, outliers¶

resolution_hours = hours from created to closed, only for closed rows whose dates make sense (closed after created, not in the future). That is our main numeric variable.

In [7]:
r = df["resolution_hours"].dropna()
q1, med, q3 = r.quantile([.25, .5, .75])
iqr = q3 - q1
lo, hi = q1 - 1.5 * iqr, q3 + 1.5 * iqr
summary = pd.Series({
    "n (valid closed rows)": len(r),
    "mean": r.mean(), "median": med, "mode (rounded to 1 h)": r.round(0).mode()[0],
    "min": r.min(), "Q1": q1, "Q3": q3, "max": r.max(), "range": r.max() - r.min(),
    "IQR": iqr, "variance": r.var(), "std dev": r.std(),
    "skewness": stats.skew(r), "lower fence": lo, "upper fence": hi,
    "outliers (count)": ((r < lo) | (r > hi)).sum(),
    "outliers (%)": ((r < lo) | (r > hi)).mean() * 100,
}).round(2)
summary.to_frame("resolution_hours")
Out[7]:
resolution_hours
n (valid closed rows) 113541.00
mean 154.56
median 7.43
mode (rounded to 1 h) 1.00
min 0.00
Q1 1.17
Q3 76.26
max 8538.45
range 8538.45
IQR 75.09
variance 224522.11
std dev 473.84
skewness 6.23
lower fence -111.47
upper fence 188.90
outliers (count) 17332.00
outliers (%) 15.26

How to read this: the mean (~155 h, about 6.5 days) is about 20 times the median (~7.4 h). That gap, plus skewness of about 6, means a long right tail: most requests close within hours, but a minority stay open for weeks or months and pull the average up. So we report the median as the "typical" time.

The log-scale histogram shows two humps: one around 1 hour (mostly NYPD calls such as parking and noise) and one around 2-4 days (inspection-type work such as housing and sanitation). The spike at the far left is the 1,927 requests closed in the same second they were opened (flag_zero_duration), which are likely auto-closed or duplicate requests. Two humps mean one "average" hides two different kinds of work.

The SQL version (T08) uses the nearest-rank method for quartiles, so it may differ from pandas in the 2nd-3rd decimal place.

sns.boxplot(data=df[df.agency.isin(top_ag) & df.resolution_hours.notna()],

Outlier policy: about 15% of valid durations sit above the upper fence (~189 h, ~8 days). That is far too many to call "errors"; they are mostly housing (HPD) and inspection-type cases that genuinely take weeks. The flag res_outlier_iqr marks them for investigation; nothing is deleted.

3. The 15 analyst investigations¶

T01. How many distinct requests are in the analysed extract?¶

In [10]:
show_sql("T01")
res = Q.run("T01", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests)
SELECT COUNT(*)                   AS total_rows,
       COUNT(DISTINCT unique_key) AS distinct_requests,
       MIN(created_date)          AS first_created,
       MAX(created_date)          AS last_created,
       COUNT(DISTINCT created_month) AS months_covered
FROM base
result rows: 1
Out[10]:
total_rows distinct_requests first_created last_created months_covered
0 119202 119202 2025-11-01 00:02:29 2026-10-31 23:53:38 12

Pattern observed: 119,202 rows, 119,202 distinct IDs, so no duplicates. 12 full months (Nov 2025 - Oct 2026).

Cautious interpretation: This is a ~3% systematic sample (IDs ending 07/37/67), not all NYC 311 traffic. Multiply by ~33 for a rough full-city scale.

Pattern observed: Volume is steady at ~9,000-10,400 per month. Closed share falls from ~98.6% (Nov 2025) to ~83.7% (Oct 2026).

Cautious interpretation: The falling closure rate is mainly a timing effect: recent requests have had less time to close. It is not evidence that agencies got slower.

Pattern observed: Weekdays are busier than weekends (Mon/Tue ~18.2k vs Sat/Sun ~15.7k). Weekday peak is 09:00-11:00 (Tuesday 10:00 is the busiest slot). Weekends flip the pattern: Saturday 22:00 and Sunday 00:00 are among the busiest hours of the week, driven by noise complaints.

Cautious interpretation: Only 112 rows have a 00:00:00 timestamp, so midnight placeholder stamps barely affect this. Useful for call-centre staffing, with care.

T08. What do valid resolution durations look like?¶

In [23]:
show_sql("T08")
res = Q.run("T08", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
r AS (
    SELECT resolution_hours AS h,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM base
    WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT MAX(cnt)                    AS n_valid,
       ROUND(AVG(h), 2)            AS mean_h,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.50 * cnt) THEN h END) AS median_h,
       MIN(h)                      AS min_h,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.25 * cnt) THEN h END) AS q1_h,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.75 * cnt) THEN h END) AS q3_h,
       MAX(h)                      AS max_h,
       ROUND(MAX(h) - MIN(h), 2)   AS range_h,
       ROUND(VAR_SAMP(h), 2)       AS variance_h2,
       ROUND(STDDEV_SAMP(h), 2)    AS std_h
FROM r

result rows: 1
Out[23]:
n_valid mean_h median_h min_h q1_h q3_h max_h range_h variance_h2 std_h
0 113541 154.56 7.432 0.0 1.171 76.264 8538.454 8538.45 224522.11 473.84
In [24]:
print("valid closed rows used (sample size):", int(df.resolution_hours.notna().sum()))

valid closed rows used (sample size): 113541

Pattern observed: 113,541 valid durations. Median 7.4 h, mean 154.6 h, Q1 1.2 h, Q3 76.3 h, max 8,538 h (~356 days), std 474 h.

Cautious interpretation: Mean far above median = strongly right-skewed. Use the median for 'typical' and the Q3/max to talk about the long tail.

T09. Which complaint categories take longest (median)?¶

In [25]:
show_sql("T09")
res = Q.run("T09", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
r AS (
    SELECT complaint_type, resolution_hours AS h,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY complaint_type ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
           COUNT(*)     OVER (PARTITION BY complaint_type) AS cnt
    FROM base
    WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT complaint_type,
       MAX(cnt) AS n_valid,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.5 * cnt) THEN h END) AS median_h,
       ROUND(AVG(h), 2) AS mean_h
FROM r
GROUP BY complaint_type
HAVING n_valid >= 50
ORDER BY median_h DESC

T10. Which agencies take longest (median)?¶

In [28]:
show_sql("T10")
res = Q.run("T10", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
r AS (
    SELECT agency, resolution_hours AS h,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY agency ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
           COUNT(*)     OVER (PARTITION BY agency) AS cnt
    FROM base
    WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT agency,
       MAX(cnt) AS n_valid,
       MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.5 * cnt) THEN h END) AS median_h,
       ROUND(AVG(h), 2) AS mean_h,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(h > 72), 2) AS over_72h_pct
FROM r
GROUP BY agency
HAVING n_valid >= 50
ORDER BY median_h DESC

result rows: 12

T11. Where are the IQR outliers?¶

In [31]:
show_sql("T11")
res = Q.run("T11", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
r AS (
    SELECT resolution_hours AS h,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
           COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM base WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
),
q AS (
    SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.25 * cnt) THEN h END) AS q1,
           MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.75 * cnt) THEN h END) AS q3
    FROM r
),
fences AS (SELECT q1, q3, q3 - q1 AS iqr,
                  q1 - 1.5 * (q3 - q1) AS lower_fence,
                  q3 + 1.5 * (q3 - q1) AS upper_fence FROM q)
SELECT b.complaint_type,
       COUNT(*) AS n_valid,
       SUM(b.resolution_hours > f.upper_fence OR b.resolution_hours < f.lower_fence) AS outliers,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(b.resolution_hours > f.upper_fence OR b.resolution_hours < f.lower_fence), 2) AS outlier_pct,
       ROUND(MAX(f.upper_fence), 2) AS upper_fence_h,
       ROUND(MAX(b.resolution_hours), 1) AS longest_h
FROM base b CROSS JOIN fences f
WHERE b.resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY b.complaint_type
HAVING outliers > 0
ORDER BY outliers DESC
LIMIT 15

T12a. How skewed is resolution time?¶

In [34]:
show_sql("T12a")
res = Q.run("T12a", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
s AS (SELECT AVG(resolution_hours) AS m, STDDEV_POP(resolution_hours) AS sd
      FROM base WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n_valid,
       ROUND(MAX(s.m), 2)  AS mean_h,
       ROUND(MAX(s.sd), 2) AS std_h,
       ROUND(AVG(POW(b.resolution_hours - s.m, 3)) / POW(MAX(s.sd), 3), 2) AS skewness
FROM base b CROSS JOIN s
WHERE b.resolution_hours IS NOT NULL

result rows: 1
Out[34]:
n_valid mean_h std_h skewness
0 113541 154.56 473.84 6.23

Pattern observed: Moment skewness = 6.23 (0 would be symmetric).

Cautious interpretation: Strong right skew: a few very long cases dominate the mean.

T12b. How are durations distributed across time buckets?¶

In [35]:
show_sql("T12b")
res = Q.run("T12b", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests)
SELECT CASE
         WHEN resolution_hours < 1   THEN '1. under 1 hour'
         WHEN resolution_hours < 4   THEN '2. 1-4 hours'
         WHEN resolution_hours < 24  THEN '3. 4-24 hours'
         WHEN resolution_hours < 72  THEN '4. 1-3 days'
         WHEN resolution_hours < 168 THEN '5. 3-7 days'
         WHEN resolution_hours < 720 THEN '6. 7-30 days'
         ELSE '7. over 30 days' END AS duration_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS requests,
       ROUND(100 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS share_pct
FROM base
WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY duration_bucket
ORDER BY duration_bucket

T13b. Where are the hotspots (~1 km cells)?¶

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
cells AS (
    SELECT ROUND(latitude, 2) AS lat_cell, ROUND(longitude, 2) AS lon_cell,
           borough, complaint_type
    FROM base
    WHERE flag_missing_coords = 0 AND flag_coords_outside_nyc = 0
),
top_type AS (
    SELECT lat_cell, lon_cell, complaint_type,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lat_cell, lon_cell ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rk
    FROM cells GROUP BY lat_cell, lon_cell, complaint_type
)
SELECT c.lat_cell, c.lon_cell, MAX(c.borough) AS borough,
       COUNT(*) AS requests,
       MAX(t.complaint_type) AS top_complaint
FROM cells c
JOIN top_type t ON t.lat_cell = c.lat_cell AND t.lon_cell = c.lon_cell AND t.rk = 1
GROUP BY c.lat_cell, c.lon_cell
ORDER BY requests DESC
LIMIT 15

T15. Which categories are both high-volume and slow?¶

In [43]:
show_sql("T15")
res = Q.run("T15", con)
print("result rows:", len(res))
res

WITH base AS (SELECT * FROM service_requests),
r AS (
    SELECT complaint_type, resolution_hours AS h,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY complaint_type ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
           COUNT(*)     OVER (PARTITION BY complaint_type) AS cnt
    FROM base WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL
),
cat AS (
    SELECT complaint_type, MAX(cnt) AS n_valid,
           MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.5 * cnt) THEN h END) AS median_h
    FROM r GROUP BY complaint_type
),
overall AS (
    SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN rn = CEIL(0.5 * cnt) THEN h END) AS overall_median_h
    FROM (SELECT resolution_hours AS h,
                 ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY resolution_hours) AS rn,
                 COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
          FROM base WHERE resolution_hours IS NOT NULL) x
),
vol AS (SELECT complaint_type, COUNT(*) AS requests,
               RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS volume_rank
        FROM base GROUP BY complaint_type)
SELECT v.complaint_type, v.requests, v.volume_rank, c.n_valid, c.median_h,
       ROUND(o.overall_median_h, 2) AS overall_median_h,
       ROUND(c.median_h / NULLIF(o.overall_median_h, 0), 1) AS times_overall_median
FROM vol v
JOIN cat c ON c.complaint_type = v.complaint_type
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE v.volume_rank <= 20 AND c.median_h > o.overall_median_h
ORDER BY c.median_h DESC

Pattern observed: Among the top-20 categories by volume, housing issues stand out: DOOR/WINDOW (313 h), UNSANITARY CONDITION (270 h), WATER LEAK (262 h), PLUMBING (218 h), PAINT/PLASTER (195 h); HEAT/HOT WATER (rank 3) at 43 h.

Cautious interpretation: These are the strongest candidates for operational attention: they are both common and slow. Complexity and access to apartments partly explain it.

4. Limitations¶

  • 311 data counts reported requests, not how common a problem really is.
  • The sample is ~3% of requests over 12 months, pulled on one date; the live dataset changes daily.
  • Recent months look less "closed" because they had less time.
  • Agencies and categories differ in complexity, so duration comparisons are not efficiency rankings.
  • "Closed" is a recorded status; it does not prove the problem was fixed or the citizen was satisfied.
  • The 72-hour cut-off is a project choice, not an official NYC service standard.
